note: PINNED and UNPINNED each deliver variable 5 as the case-equivalent literals First and first of one 2020 edition, and each literal's member carries two code lists that disagree on its code's label. Each register's per-column [[representation.parallel]] entry therefore reports two unsupported_representation_coding errors that share code, subject, refs, fields and period and differ only in their detail and withheld output (the literal), as the old test's `issue` and `other` did (its [output] and [detail] params are one construction here). From the old test: an entry without a diagnostic digest matches both and is over-broad, leaving both errors (UNPINNED); one entry per issue, each pinning its issue's complete diagnostic, acknowledges exactly that issue (PINNED; old: `acknowledged == {code: 2}`, every copy a warning, `acknowledged_by` the matching entry). Each `expected_diagnostic_sha256` is the canonical SHA-256 of the issue as the build's report ledger records it before it is acknowledged, copied as a curator copies it; no placeholder renders it, because the diagnostic exists only after a build. The case shows the copy is right: a wrong digest leaves that issue an error and the entry stale (`acknowledge-guarded-stale-when-its-diagnostic-digest-differs`, which is also the old test's drift arm).
fails_if: `resolve_source_scope` (source_scope.py) leaves `expected_diagnostic_sha256` out of the held issue key, or stops hashing the complete diagnostic for coordinates a guarded entry names, so PINNED's two entries collide or match neither issue (one issue is acknowledged twice, or both entries go stale); or the settle loop stops counting distinct matches, so UNPINNED's undigested entry acknowledges one of its two issues instead of being over-broad

sources.description: Variable 5 (Income) delivers the case-equivalent literals First and first as two members of one 2020 edition in PINNED (register 1: members 600, 601) and UNPINNED (register 2: members 700, 701). Each member carries two lists that disagree on its one code's label, so no literal has one complete finite domain.
